title: Mixtures and Separation
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Mixtures and Separation Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Everyday materials are often mixtures: pure substances and mixtures, heterogeneous mixtures, and separating mixtures by particle size (sifting, filtering) and density (settling, flotation), including in industry and mining. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 6, Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 science worksheets (BC): pure substances and mixtures, heterogeneous and homogeneous mixtures, sieving, filtering, settling and magnetism. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods.
body_html:
How to think about it

A pure substance has only one kind of particle; a mixture has two or more. In a heterogeneous mixture you can see the different parts, like gravel and sand or oil and water.

Mixtures are separated by differences in their parts: sieving and filtering use particle size, settling and flotation use density, and a magnet pulls out iron. Mines use these methods to separate valuable minerals from rock.

Example

How can you separate sand from water?

Sand particles are bigger than the holes in paper.

Answer: filter it

Example

Oil floats on water. Which property separates them?

Which one is less dense?

Answer: density

Common mistakes

  • Thinking you can filter out dissolved salt.
  • Calling salt water a heterogeneous mixture (it is a solution).
  • Forgetting that a magnet only picks up iron, nickel and cobalt.

items.q: What is a saturated solution?

items.q: How can you separate a mixture of dried beans and flour?

c: So that the dyes do not dissolve straight into the solvent in the beaker.

So that the dyes move faster.
